provenance.tool: Sound Equalization and Correction System 2 (SECS 2) Beta 1.1.0, Speaker Gallery (DCinside), GPL-3.0
provenance.exporter: tests/migration/export_goldens_secs2.py (no SECS code; calls the oracle and records its results)
provenance.numpy_dispatch: SIMD above the X86-64-v2 baseline disabled: the oracle's float64 transcendental functions are the C library's
provenance.configuration: mains = the listed speakers, no subwoofers, no crossover; positions = ear positions in order (position 1 is SECS's listening position); main_weight sets SECS MAIN_WEIGHT and MAIN_WEIGHT_LO; modes from SECS MODES, ultra-<ms> from its ultra mode; target flat (0 dB) or the demo room-target.csv interpolated linearly in Hz with end values held. In all/mixed the oracle places every speaker on one time origin (the earliest onset at position 1 over all seven); its responses therefore are not the per-speaker responses and only its gains and levels are a reference.

ir.construction: examples/secs2_inputs omni/*: open_recording_samples(estimator, fs, tracks, speakers, side, 2.0), uncropped (391270 samples)

fields.mag_db: 20*log10(|F|+1e-12) of the channel correction (FIR and PEQ) at bins, 10 significant digits
